skill.name: pytest
skill.description: Guidance for writing, organizing, and running Python tests with pytest.
skill.summary: Write practical pytest tests with fixtures, parametrization, async patterns, markers, and common integration examples.
skill.author: bossjones

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, pytest examples, dummy environment variables, and ordinary test data. One high-severity issue remains: the documentation includes an eval(input) example that teaches unsafe dynamic code execution, even though the shown inputs are hardcoded.

remediation.issue: Unsafe eval example in parametrized pytest documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Replace eval(input) with a small arithmetic function, operator mapping, or explicit expected values that do not execute strings as code.

remediation.issue: Shell command examples may be misclassified by automated scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Label command examples as user-run documentation and avoid formatting that resembles executable embedded scripts.

remediation.issue: Placeholder API key examples can trigger secret detectors.
remediation.suggestion: Use names such as TEST_TOKEN and values such as dummy-value to make clear that no real credential is present.

content.user_title: Write Better Python Tests with pytest
content.value_statement: Python test suites can become hard to organize as projects grow. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical pytest patterns for fixtures, parametrization, async tests, markers, and integration testing.
actual_capabilities: Explains basic pytest test structure and command examples.
Shows fixture setup, teardown, scope, and shared conftest patterns.
Provides parametrization examples for multiple inputs and combinations.
Covers async tests and async fixtures with pytest markers.
Demonstrates markers, API tests, database tests, and exception assertions.
Lists pytest-related development requirements and optional plugins.
limitations: It is a reference guide, not an installed pytest plugin.
It does not inspect project-specific test failures by itself.
Some examples use placeholder application functions that must already exist.
One parametrization example should avoid eval before reuse in production tests.

use_cases.title: Add tests to a Python feature
use_cases.description: Use fixture and assertion examples to build clear unit tests for new code paths.

use_cases.title: Organize shared test setup
use_cases.description: Use conftest, fixture scope, and teardown patterns to reduce repeated setup code.

use_cases.title: Expand integration coverage
use_cases.description: Use API, database, async, marker, and exception examples to plan broader pytest coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a first pytest test.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pytest skill to write a simple test for this Python function. Include clear assertions and explain where the test file should live.

prompt_templates.title: Add Fixtures
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pytest skill to refactor these repeated setup steps into fixtures. Include setup, teardown, and recommended fixture scope.

prompt_templates.title: Parametrize Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pytest skill to convert these repeated tests into parametrized tests. Avoid eval and keep each case explicit and safe.

prompt_templates.title: Design Test Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a full testing plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pytest skill to design a test strategy for this Python service. Include fixtures, async tests, markers, API tests, database tests, and failure cases.

output_examples.input: Request: Add pytest coverage for a utility function that formats user names.
output_examples.output: A concise test module with descriptive test names, direct assertions, and a small parametrized table for common name formats.

output_examples.input: Request: Reduce repeated database setup across several tests.
output_examples.output: A fixture-based layout that creates the test database, yields a session to each test, and closes resources after each test finishes.

output_examples.input: Request: Separate slow integration tests from fast unit tests.
output_examples.output: A marker plan with unit, integration, and slow groups, plus command examples for running or excluding each group.

best_practices: Keep tests small, named for behavior, and focused on one expected outcome.
Use fixtures for shared setup, and choose the narrowest useful fixture scope.
Parametrize repeated cases with explicit inputs and expected outputs.
anti_patterns: Do not use eval or dynamic code execution to compute expected test results.
Do not hide broad setup side effects inside fixtures with unclear scope.
Do not mix slow integration tests with fast unit tests without markers.

faq.question: Does this skill install pytest?
faq.answer: No. It gives pytest guidance and examples. You still install pytest in your project environment.

faq.question: Can it help with async tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes async test and async fixture patterns, including pytest markers used for asynchronous code.

faq.question: Does it cover fixtures?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers basic fixtures, setup and teardown, fixture scopes, and shared fixtures in conftest.py.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it for test refactoring?
faq.answer: Yes. Claude Code and Codex can use the examples to refactor repeated setup into pytest fixtures and parametrized tests.

faq.question: Is it safe to copy every example as written?
faq.answer: No. Review examples before reuse. The eval example should be replaced with a safer explicit calculation pattern.

faq.question: What types of tests are included?
faq.answer: It includes unit tests, fixture-based tests, parametrized tests, async tests, API tests, database tests, and error handling tests.
